subject_line: The vacant Midwestern lots in Department of Elegy
email_body:
Dear Mary,

I've been reading about Department of Elegy and its dim nightclubs, churning lakes and vacant Midwestern lots, held together by the recurring "Book" poems. I was struck that one reader called it both nostalgic and anti-nostalgic at once.

I'd love to ask how you kept that balance: how you decide when a remembered place gets tenderness and when it gets resisted.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is built from a few written questions that you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
